originalControls.scope: Native reg, net and integer handle metadata with scalar, ascending, descending, negative and 73-bit ranges; existing bit caches preserve normalized index mappings. Explicit late native net construction/admission gets a fresh handle identity while sharing a live node. Unsupported two-state, real, array, array-word, constant and foreign handles refuse admission before and after growth without changing admitted state. No board-created alias, handle deletion, automatic-scope admission or operational qualification is inferred.

priorCallbackControls.scope: Native callback allocation/lifetime, typed signal handoff, registered node and adjusted owner/filter linkage agree with independent full inventories. Unadmitted objects, foreign/mismatched node/filter/object pointers and active traversal refuse before output. Restored faults preserve continuation; cancelled callbacks remain linked until native deletion. This fixture does not qualify board integration, aggregate runtime cost or general rollback.

originalControls.scope: All six paired metadata fault APIs restore exact native signal/callback/graph state. Wrong field or handle restoration attempts refuse without losing the pending fault, and mutation during active callback traversal refuses. Original and instrumented callback/value continuation agrees. Combined startup faults and operational campaign qualification remain separate.

scope: Optimized and reference native inventories produce identical complete bytes and return codes in the same process, including metadata faults, restored lifetimes, active callbacks, range/cache growth and rejected automatic scopes. Empty admission still emits an empty image even with an automatic scope. This establishes differential controls, not operational cost or whole-board qualification.
